claims.statement: Poland had 1,631,400 prosumer installations at the end of April 2026 and 127,386 prosumer storage systems at the end of March 2026, creating a large installed base but a much smaller storage-led initial segment.
Official Polish guidance identifies self-consumption and storage management as core net-billing levers and describes hourly-price scheduling, so the optimisation trigger is real.

URE's 2026 approved household tariff averages 495.16 PLN/MWh for the energy component and reports 1.8 MWh average annual G11 consumption, so a 180-420 PLN annual software fee is a demanding household denominator unless flexible-load savings or installer value is directly measured.

SolarEdge already bundles tariff-, weather-, load- and battery-aware optimisation, device scheduling and homeowner control in SolarEdge ONE, making a generic optimiser reproducible and vulnerable to OEM bundling.

OEM data access is technically possible but commercially and operationally gated: SolarEdge documents rate limits, while Fronius restricts productive Solar.web Query API access to contracted business partners and charges by data package.

The EU Data Act supports a user's ability to request readily available connected-product data for a chosen third party, but it does not create a personal-data legal basis, eliminate security or trade-secret controls, or confer remote-control and firmware-alteration rights.

A savings report needs an explicit measurement boundary and baseline method because whole-site bills mix the intervention with weather, occupancy and other changes; the artifact is not defensible merely because an optimisation model is useful.

contrary_evidence: SolarEdge ONE already performs the core tariff-, weather-, load- and battery-aware optimisation and controls devices inside its ecosystem.
Fronius offers a professional API for monitoring, O&M, smart-home and control uses, so an OEM or platform can bundle much of the data layer.

The average G11 household's energy-supply component makes the proposed annual software fee material before distribution, taxes and fixed charges; the addressable value is concentrated in higher-consumption flexible-load homes.
The Data Act improves user-directed data access but does not grant remote-control, firmware or warranty authority and retains GDPR, security and trade-secret constraints.
A protocol library and AI-generated optimiser are reproducible; durable value must come from permissioned integrations, longitudinal interventions and installer adoption of the report.

economics.acquisition_route: Use 30-50 authorised sites from the family company to run shadow recommendations and pre-specified baseline tests for one inverter family, then seek three unrelated installers who pay for the same report. Do not count wholesalers or buying groups as distribution until a referral or resale commitment exists.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Not established by current evidence. A scenario hurdle is 20000 paid sites at 20 PLN monthly net revenue, or 4.8m PLN recurring annual revenue before diagnostics. At an assumed 25% after-tax owner-cash margin after operating reinvestment, that is about 1.2m PLN yearly and would require roughly five mature years to accumulate 5m PLN, excluding business equity and before ramp. The paid-site count, margin and retention are all unvalidated and must not be double-counted with a valuation.
economics.founder_time: Three to four hours per day is feasible for one read-only adapter and one installer pilot if the family company performs customer support and every equipment change. Remote control, several OEMs or direct homeowner support would require added staff or a narrower scope before launch.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Read-only ingestion, models and reports can support roughly 70-85% software gross margin after OEM API, hosting and support costs once an adapter is stable. Early multi-vendor integration, bill normalisation and installer support are implementation work and can reduce blended gross margin below 60%; this must be measured in the pilot.
economics.payback: Buyer payback is not established. A recurring installer licence should be accepted only if one avoided diagnostic visit or one incremental profitable retrofit covers at least twelve months of fees; a homeowner audit should be priced below conservatively measured bill savings, not forecast savings.
economics.pricing: Test rather than assume: 300-700 PLN for a one-off homeowner diagnostic and 10-25 PLN per authorised site per month for an installer workflow, with any retrofit referral fee disclosed. At 15-35 PLN monthly, the original recurring fee would equal 180-420 PLN per year, a material share of the average household's 2026 energy-supply component, so the first paid segment should have batteries or other flexible high loads and a concrete installer event.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Seasonal bills, tariffs, faults and retrofit decisions recur, but free OEM scheduling and monitoring can absorb routine use. Retention therefore depends on cross-vendor evidence, installer workflow history and proven avoided labour or incremental retrofit conversion.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned device-protocol library plus longitudinal Polish load, tariff, weather and intervention-response data can reduce integration time and improve counterfactual estimates, but only if OEM access remains lawful and paid installers contribute repeated cases.
fingerprint.customer: Polish installers with a material installed base of residential prosumer sites, initially households that combine PV with batteries, heat pumps or EV charging and whose equipment exposes authorised read access.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot through the founder's family installation company, prove one inverter-family workflow and measured installer value, then sell directly to comparable installers; wholesaler or buying-group distribution remains an unvalidated second channel.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: White-label, read-first software that imports authorised meter and inverter history, models tariff and weather effects, compares baseline and intervention periods, and produces a versioned optimisation or retrofit report; per-site installer SaaS plus fixed-price diagnostics, with referral revenue only where transparently disclosed.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays for per-site monitoring or a decision report when triaging a service call or qualifying a retrofit; the prosumer may pay for a one-off audit, but recurring homeowner willingness to pay is unproven.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A prosumer receives a disappointing bill, considers a battery or EMS retrofit, or asks the installer whether existing equipment is scheduled well under net-billing, creating a service or retrofit decision that needs quantified evidence.

founder_fit: The family renewable-energy company provides an unusually credible, low-social-cost route to a bounded pilot and access to installer workflows.
Forecasting, counterfactual measurement and tariff simulation fit the founder's data-science strengths.
A read-first product with all physical or control changes executed by qualified installers limits safety exposure and is compatible with continued employment.
The founder must hold the scope to one protocol and installer-facing support; multi-OEM homeowner support would exceed the stated part-time envelope.
risks: Poor advice or unapproved control could increase bills, reduce comfort, accelerate battery degradation or create warranty and safety disputes.
OEM API terms, quotas, pricing or account permissions can strand an adapter or eliminate margin.
Savings claims without a documented baseline can create consumer-protection and installer-liability exposure.
OEMs can bundle optimisation and installer dashboards, leaving the product without a scarce control point.
Multi-vendor edge cases and homeowner support can turn a software product into an incompatible part-time services business.

structure.commercial_archetype: Installer-channel energy-analytics SaaS with paid diagnostics and retrofit-decision support
structure.control_point: The versioned baseline, intervention and ROI report an installer uses to approve a configuration change, avoid a truck roll or recommend a retrofit
structure.critical_dependency: Authorised, sufficiently granular meter and inverter data plus installer acceptance of the report as a paid operational decision artifact; remote device control is not assumed

thesis: Give Polish PV, battery and heat-pump installers a vendor-neutral, read-first monitoring and decision layer that uses authorised meter and inverter data to identify losses under net-billing, compare a documented baseline with an intervention, and issue a retrofit or configuration report the installer can stand behind. The commercial wedge is the installer-paid decision and verification workflow around service calls and hardware retrofits, not a generic optimisation algorithm or another homeowner dashboard.
title: White-Label PV Self-Consumption Optimizer for Installers
uncertainties: Incremental bill savings over OEM defaults and simple schedules are unknown and require a pre-specified field test.
Installer willingness to pay for recurring monitoring, avoided truck rolls or retrofit qualification is unknown.
Account-level API permission, commercial reuse rights, control rights and warranty treatment differ by OEM and remain unknown beyond the documented examples.
The number of Polish sites combining batteries or other controllable high loads with supported devices and installers willing to participate is unknown.
Wholesaler, buying-group and installer referral channels are hypotheses with no commitment evidence.
The 20000-site wealth scenario, contribution margin and renewal rate are assumptions rather than market evidence.
